references.text: Melchizedek blesses God Most High with the same formula of praise ('Blessed be...') that Eliezer uses in Gen 24:27.
God's promises to Abraham about blessing form the basis for Eliezer's mission and his gratitude for God's faithful guidance in Gen 24:27.
Eliezer praises the Lord again for leading him on the right path to find a wife for Isaac, repeating themes of God's faithful guidance from verse 27.
Jacob uses the same key words 'chesed' (steadfast love) and 'emet' (faithfulness) when he thanks God for all the goodness shown to his servant—a direct parallel to Eliezer's wording in Gen 24:27.
God confirms His faithfulness to Isaac for Abraham's sake, showing God's enduring grace toward Abraham's family, as Eliezer acknowledges in Gen 24:27.
Naomi blesses the Lord and recognizes that His 'chesed' (steadfast love/faithfulness) has not ceased, paralleling Eliezer's praise for God's faithfulness in Gen 24:27.
David's trust that the Lord's goodness and mercy will follow him all his days resonates with Eliezer's experience of God's faithful guidance in Gen 24:27.
Same event: Eliezer's prayer before (24:12) and thanksgiving after (24:27) God's guidance.
Same event: Eliezer's prayer for guidance (24:42) before the confirmation in 24:27.
Causal link: God's plan for Abraham's household (18:19) is carried out through Eliezer's journey (24:27).
Causal link: The covenant (17:9) is the foundation for Eliezer's experience of guidance (24:27).
Thematic parallel: God's guidance in Abraham's lineage (Eliezer and Jacob).
Same event: Eliezer's thanks for God's guidance (24:27) and his desire to move on (24:56).
Thematic parallel: God's guidance on 'the way' (Eliezer and Isaiah).
Thematic parallel: God's faithfulness to Abraham's lineage in dangerous situations (Eliezer and Jacob).
